sources.title: Paolo Saracco, Notes on Hopf Modules, Integrals and Frobenius Hopf Algebras (course notes, 2019)
sources.locator: §3, Theorem 3.6 and its proof (PDF pp. 15–17); §4.1, Lemma 4.2 and Proposition 4.18 (PDF pp. 19–26); §4.2, Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.5 (PDF pp. 20–21); §4.3, Proposition 4.13, Lemma 4.20, and Theorem 4.22 (PDF pp. 23–29)

contents.name: §3, Definition 3.1–3.2: left/right integrals in an augmented algebra and integral functionals in the dual
§3, Theorem 3.6 and proof: finite-dual right action, coaction, and Hopf-module compatibility
§4.1, Lemma 4.2; §4.2, Proposition 4.18 and Remark 4.19: one-dimensional integral spaces and finite-dimensional antipode bijectivity from the Hopf-module isomorphism
§4.3, Proposition 4.13: Frobenius systems and equivalent nondegenerate associative-pairing characterizations
§4.3, Theorem 4.22 and Theorem 4.24: a finite projective Hopf algebra is Frobenius when its dual has a nonzero integral, with explicit Frobenius homomorphism and Casimir data
§4.2, Lemma 4.4 and Theorem 4.5: a normalized left integral yields a Casimir element and the semisimplicity criterion
§4.2, Theorem 4.5's separability-equivalence branch and §4.3's general finite-projective reconstruction formulas
contents.reason: The local scope proves the finite-dimensional semisimplicity criterion and the Frobenius pairing directly; it does not claim separability equivalences over general rings or general finite-projective reconstruction formulas.

sources.title: Erasmus Mini-Course on Hopf Algebras (lecture notes)
sources.locator: Lecture 6, Theorems 6.2–6.4 and Definition 6.5 (PDF pp. 14–16); Lecture 7, Theorem 7.1 (PDF pp. 17–18)

contents.name: Lecture 6, definitions preceding Theorem 6.3: left/right integrals and the dual convolution integral convention
Lecture 6, page 16: the dual coaction characterization and right action on H*; Theorem 6.3(1) states the Hopf-module structure
Lecture 6, Theorem 6.3(2)–(3) and proof: one-dimensional integrals and bijective antipode
Lecture 6, Theorem 6.4 and Definition 6.5: finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras and nondegenerate associative forms
Lecture 6, Theorem 6.3(4) and the following discussion: an integral in H* gives a module isomorphism H to H* and a Frobenius conclusion
Lecture 7, Theorem 7.1 and proof: semisimplicity iff a normalized left integral exists, by splitting and averaging
Lecture 6, Theorem 6.3(1) leaves verification of the dual Hopf-module structure to the reader; Lecture 7 says to check H-linearity of the averaging map
Lecture 7, Theorem 7.2: the characteristic-zero Larson–Radford equivalence involving H*, semisimplicity, and S²=id
contents.reason: The page makes no claim that H* is semisimple or that S²=id in arbitrary characteristic; the characteristic-zero theorem is only retained as an explicit boundary warning.
